why_this_one: 18 placements. A wall bracket: planking, a flame, and a carved stone face - copra_gate is a gargoyle, which is what the fire sits in.
additive_from: A departure, and a small one. The client marks only the bonfire's flame as a blend mesh, and these sheets are flame painted on black exactly as that one is - drawn opaquely they are black rectangles with an orange smudge. The client gets away with it because its own fire at these placements is a particle effect CreateFire puts there and the mesh is the housing; this has no particles yet, so the painted flame is all there is and it has to read as one.
emitters_from: WorldObjectCatalog.cs's Fire(): luminance 0.6 to 1.1, weighted (L, 0.6L, 0.4L) for the orange, four tiles of reach. The rate and smoothing are the old port's correction rather than the client's - it redraws the luminance every rendered frame, which on a light rather than a texture is a strobe, so 3 Hz eased over an eighth of a second is the pool of light breathing at the pace a fire moves.
cutout_note: fire_light_01 carries a real alpha channel cutting away 65%, and is deliberately not declared a cut-out: it is declared additive instead, and additive supersedes. A glow is blended rather than masked - it has no edge to cut along, and its own brightness is its alpha. Declaring both got a MASK material overwritten by a BLEND one and tripped tests/cutouts.py, which was right to complain about a claim the file did not honour.
